sources.entry: LiveCodes ⚠ - Feature-rich client-side code playground for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, Typescript, Python, Go, Ruby, PHP and 90+ other languages. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: LiveCodes is a free, open-source, client-side code playground supporting React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, TypeScript, Python, Go, Ruby, PHP and 90+ other languages and frameworks, with an embeddable SDK.
summary.what_it_does: It is a browser-based code playground where code runs client-side with no server setup, install, or build step required. It supports 90+ languages, frameworks and processors, and lets users import modules from npm, deno.land/x, jsr, GitHub and other sources. Projects can be imported, exported, shared, and backed up or restored. Developer tools include a console, compiled code viewer, test runner, intellisense, and code formatting. The README also describes an SDK (npm package livecodes, with wrappers for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, Preact and web components) for embedding playgrounds in other pages and generating shareable playground URLs. Self-hosting is done by putting a downloaded release on a static file server.
use_cases: Prototyping front-end code in the browser
Trying out React, Vue, Svelte or Solid snippets
Embedding an interactive code playground in a web page
Sharing runnable code examples via links
Running small Python, Go, Ruby or PHP snippets without local installs
Self-hosting a code playground on a static file server
how_to_run: Self-hosted: download a release from the project's releases
Put the release files on any static file server
Then call createPlayground('#container', {...}) from the livecodes package in your page
stack: React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, Preact wrappers
notable: Runs entirely client-side with no servers, databases, or accounts required
Imports modules from npm, deno.land/x, jsr and GitHub
Embeddable SDK with framework wrappers and programmatic control
Can be self-hosted as static files, including GitHub Pages deployment
caveats: A GitHub account is required only for features that use GitHub Integration
Self-hosting requires downloading a release and serving static files; the README links to a separate guide for setup
